subject: mathematics
question_text: If f(x) = 2x − 1, g(x) = (x + 1)/2 for all x ∈ R, find (i) (gof)(x) (ii) (fog)(x).

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.79 — VSAQ chapter 14 Functions, question 89. The book prints NO internal mark split on its VSAQ pages (unlike its LAQ/SAQ pages): the 1+1 across the two steps is our division of the 2 marks, not the source's. Appearance years are the book's, board-split. Publisher's claims until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find both compositions — which function acts first in each, and what they simplify to.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find (gof)(x)
steps.margin_note: One mark. f acts first here, so substitute 2x − 1 into g and simplify all the way.
steps.memory_tip: In gof, f acts FIRST: substitute 2x − 1 into g and simplify all the way.

recall.must_convey: That f acts first, so 2x − 1 goes into g, and the algebra simplifies to x.
accept: g of f of x is g of two x minus one which is two x minus one plus one over two equals x
substitute two x minus one into g and it simplifies to x
the plus one cancels the minus one so you get two x over two which is x
two x minus one ni g lo petti simplify chesthe x vasthundi

steps.why: These two functions undo each other, so the composition collapses to x. Showing the cancellation is what earns the mark, not the final letter.
common_mistakes: Substituting into f instead of g.
Stopping at (2x − 1 + 1)/2 without simplifying to x.

steps.label: Find (fog)(x)
steps.margin_note: The second mark. Now g acts first. Both answers are x, which is the point of the question.
steps.memory_tip: Now g acts first. Both come to x — the two functions undo each other, which is the point.

recall.must_convey: That g acts first, (x + 1)/2 goes into f, and this also simplifies to x — so both compositions equal x.
accept: f of g of x is two times x plus one over two minus one which is x
substitute x plus one over two into f and the two cancels giving x plus one minus one equals x
both compositions give x so they are inverse functions
fog of x is also x

steps.why: Both compositions giving x is exactly the test for a pair of inverse functions — the answer is worth stating, not just computing.
common_mistakes: Writing 'same as (i)' instead of doing the second substitution.
Cancelling the 2 wrongly and leaving x + 1.

insider_note: Both compositions collapse to x, and that is the point: these two functions are inverses of each other. Getting x for one and something else for the other means an arithmetic slip, not a real asymmetry.
